title: The GDACS feed's own episode membership has been perfectly static for seven consecutive committed nights -- the longest such streak in this observatory's history -- and for the last four of those nights not one of its 93 open episodes carries GDACS's own iscurrent=true flag, a field practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py has never read
statement: Comparing (eventid, eventtype, episodeid) triples across every pair of consecutive preserved foreknown/snapshots/<date>/gdacs.json files in this observatory's full 33-night history, the set GDACS returns has been byte-identical in composition -- zero triples added, zero removed -- across all six transitions from 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-14 (09-08->09-09, 09-09->09-10, 09-10->09-11, 09-11->09-12, 09-12->09-13, 09-13->09-14). That is seven consecutive committed nights of unchanged membership. No other span in the preserved record reaches that length: the next-longest is three nights (08-28, 08-29, 08-30, i.e. two consecutive zero/zero transitions), and every other zero/zero transition in the record is isolated between nights that do add or remove triples. Within this frozen-membership span, properties.iscurrent -- a field GDACS itself sets per feature and this observatory's gdacs_futures() (practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py, lines 61-101) never reads, joins to TRACKED_FIELDS, or writes into the registry -- has collapsed to zero 'true' features and stayed there: foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-11/gdacs.json through 2026-09-14/gdacs.json each carry 93 features, all 93 read iscurrent=='false'. Every other night in the 33-night record has at least one iscurrent=='true' feature except a single isolated night, 2026-08-20 (92 features, 0 true), which recovered to 1 true the very next night. The current streak -- 2026-09-11, 09-12, 09-13, 09-14 -- is four consecutive nights, four times the only precedent, and (per this pass's own reading of the committed record) still open as of the newest snapshot. The last feature to carry iscurrent=='true' before the streak began was gdacs-fl-1104081 (Flood in China, episode 17, datemodified 2026-09-06T06:23:52) in foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-10/gdacs.json; in foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-11/gdacs.json onward the same feature (same episodeid 17, same datemodified) reads iscurrent=='false'. foreknown/registry.json's gdacs-fl-1104081 entry shows no REVISED event since 2026-09-06 and is not itself surprising (window.to 2026-09-07 has since passed, so it is independently overdue under the existing cold-start/drift split), but the flip from the feed's last true record to zero true records, with membership otherwise completely static, is the new fact. autonomy/log.jsonl's foreknown-notary-run entries for 2026-09-10 through 2026-09-14 record revised: 5 and notarized: 7-19 every night, but every one of those notarizations and revisions in this span is attributable to NWS (the id namespace nws-*) or to the two already-tracked rolling droughts extending window.to by exactly one day (the same mechanism sensor-drought-window-class-crossing.json classifies as class rolling) -- a direct scan of foreknown/registry.json shows zero GDACS futures with announced_at dated 2026-09-10 through 2026-09-14. By every field this observatory's registry tracks, GDACS has been silent for a week; by the one field it does not track, GDACS has been silent for even that week's own well-established baseline (some open episode reads as freshly attended-to on all but two of the prior 31 nights) has now itself gone quiet for four nights running.
method: For each of the 33 preserved foreknown/snapshots/<date>/gdacs.json files, loaded the GeoJSON, built the set of (properties.eventid, properties.eventtype, properties.episodeid) triples, and diffed each night against the next to count additions and removals; found the six-transition, seven-night run of zero/zero from 2026-09-08 through 2026-09-14 and confirmed no longer run exists anywhere else in the 33-night history (next longest: three nights, 08-28 through 08-30). Independently counted properties.iscurrent value frequencies ('true'/'false', string-valued) per night across all 33 snapshots, found 77 true occurrences and 3064 false occurrences overall, and located the two zero-true nights in the record (2026-08-20, isolated; 2026-09-11 through 2026-09-14, a still-open four-night run). Identified the single iscurrent=='true' feature in foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-10/gdacs.json (gdacs-fl-1104081) and confirmed the same episode (matched by episodeid and datemodified) reads iscurrent=='false' in every subsequent snapshot through 2026-09-14, cross-checked against its foreknown/registry.json entry (last REVISED 2026-09-06, no REAPPEARED, no CLOSED_BY_SOURCE). Read practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py's gdacs_futures() in full to confirm iscurrent is not among the properties read into a future record, and practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py's TRACKED_FIELDS and update_registry() to confirm closure is decided solely by a future id's absence from observed, never by iscurrent. Cross-checked autonomy/log.jsonl's foreknown-notary-run entries for 2026-09-10 through 2026-09-14 against foreknown/registry.json's announced_at field to confirm zero GDACS notarizations fall in that span (all of that span's notarized/revised counts are NWS ids or the two already-tracked rolling droughts). Ran python -m pip install -e ./practice, python -m pytest practice/tests, python stage/generate.py --repo-root ., and python verify.py --repo-root . after writing this file; all green, no code changed.

iscurrent_zero_true_streaks.status: open as of newest committed snapshot 2026-09-14

worth_watching_because: This observatory's own registry can only ever learn that a GDACS episode changed by watching four fields (severity, window, what, where); it has no way to represent 'the source looked at this record and confirmed nothing changed' versus 'the source has not looked at this record at all', which is exactly the gap sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json was proposed to close (it never got past PROPOSED because two prior reviews found the underlying datemodified signal too batchy and too echo-prone to threshold safely). Tonight's finding is a different angle on the same blind spot, on a different unread field: not one record's staleness, but the whole feed's population of 'the source currently marks this as its live case' collapsing to zero and staying there for the longest span this observatory has ever preserved, at the same time as the feed's very composition stopped changing at all for the longest span it has ever preserved. Two independently-computed signals moving together and both hitting an unprecedented extreme at once is more than either alone; it is exactly the kind of thing that would either be explained a night or two from now by GDACS resuming normal issuance (in which case this was a quiet weekend-shaped lull, visible only because nothing before now made the observatory look at iscurrent's population as a whole), or would keep extending, which the existing sensor's own falsification clause already treats as live-signal evidence rather than noise.
left_alone: Not proposing a new sensor: like sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's own two prior reviews, this is one instance of one shape (a population-level collapse, not yet a per-record test_rule) with no second occurrence yet to threshold a streak length against -- the four-night run could still be this week's ordinary lull. Not adding a review entry to sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json itself: that proposal's test_rule and falsification clause are built around per-record datemodified staleness (days_since_datemodified_changed), not the whole-feed iscurrent population this observation measures, and folding a differently-shaped finding into that file's review history would blur what its own test_rule is actually being judged against; this stays a freestanding observation the maintainer or a future pass can connect explicitly if the pattern recurs. Not editing gdacs_futures() to read or record iscurrent: a field this observatory has never stored has no history to compare against beyond what tonight's scan of preserved snapshot bytes already recovered, and deciding whether to start recording it is exactly the kind of scope decision sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's own falsification clause already reserves for a promotion, not a repair. Checked and left unchanged: sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json (gdacs-tc-1001305 -- itself one of the 93 iscurrent=='false' features in tonight's snapshot -- still OPEN, history unchanged since its last REVISED on 2026-09-03, no second closure); memoryhole/readings/2026-09-13.json, the newest reading, carries zero rule-layer abstentions (entries[].abstentions empty on all 47 entries), so no verdicts file is due tonight. registry-stall-check ran clean this morning (autonomy/log.jsonl, 2026-09-15T05:58:39+00:00, stale: []).
